prompt: I'm about to start on a multi-tenant billing module but I still haven't decided per-seat vs usage-based pricing, how proration works mid-cycle, or whether invoices live in Stripe or our own DB. Before I write a line, push on whatever I haven't nailed down.
why: Undecided design decisions before building; user wants them settled.

prompt:
Pasting our plan for moving off Heroku onto Fly.io below. The team starts next Monday. What am I missing? Poke holes in it.

1. Dockerize all 4 apps
2. Move Postgres via pg_dump/restore over a weekend
3. Swap DNS
4. Kill Heroku
why: Challenge a plan and find gaps; no code to review.

prompt: we want offline mode in the react native app. nobody has decided conflict resolution, what gets cached, or for how long. can you walk me through those one at a time so we actually land on something
why: Interview to settle open design decisions one by one.

prompt: Play devil's advocate. My plan is to replace all 30 of our cron jobs with a self-hosted Temporal cluster next sprint. Tear into it before I pitch it to the CTO.
why: Asks to be challenged on a plan.

prompt: Designing the permission model for our internal admin tool. Still torn between plain roles and attribute-based rules, and haven't figured out inheritance or what we audit. Keep asking me hard questions until it's settled, then write down what we chose.
why: Unsettled design; wants questioning until decided and decisions recorded.

prompt: The nightly ETL reports 1,204,331 rows loaded into staging but the warehouse fact table only gets 1,198,870 for the same date. No errors anywhere in the logs. What's eating the rows?
why: Data discrepancy between two numbers that should match, cause unknown.

prompt: checkout.spec.ts passes every single time on my machine but times out on GitHub Actions maybe 1 run in 5. I've rerun it like 20 times. Help me figure out what's different.
why: Flaky CI-only failure.

prompt: Since we bumped the API containers from Node 20 to Node 22, p99 latency jumped from ~180ms to ~900ms. As far as I know nothing else in that deploy changed.
why: Regression/slowdown after an upgrade with unknown cause.

prompt: Our Android app crashes on launch, but only on Samsung Galaxy A-series phones running Android 13. Crashlytics shows a SIGSEGV inside libsqlite. Pixels and iPhones are totally fine. Any idea?
why: Device-specific crash, cause unknown.

prompt: I shipped the patch for the leak in the thumbnail worker last Tuesday and it STILL gets OOM-killed after about six hours. Why??
why: A fix that did not work; leak/OOM.

prompt: The fix for the double-charge bug is merged and deployed to staging. Before I email the customer saying it's resolved, make sure it actually is resolved on staging.
why: Confirm a deployed fix works against the real system before claiming done.

prompt: I think the CSV export feature is finished. Can you run it end to end and confirm it produces the file with the right columns and row count? Don't just read the code.
why: Check finished work against the real artifact.

prompt: Added the Strict-Transport-Security header to the nginx config and reloaded it on prod. Is it actually being sent now?
why: Confirm a config change took effect on a deployed system.

prompt: I flipped the new_onboarding flag to 10% rollout in LaunchDarkly about an hour ago. Can you check it really took effect for the staging app?
why: Confirm a config/flag change took effect.

prompt: You told me the pagination bug was fixed three messages ago. Show me, don't tell me - run the thing and paste me the output.
why: Demand for evidence that claimed-done work works.

prompt: I'm renaming the user_id column to account_id on the orders table and updated the SQLAlchemy model to match. Is anything else going to fall over when I ship this?
why: Concrete persisted-schema change; what breaks elsewhere.

prompt: We're moving pydantic from v1 to v2 inside common-lib, which six of our services import. What's likely to break across those services?
why: Dependency upgrade in a shared package; impact on consumers.

prompt: Small PR: flips the default of retry_on_timeout from True to False in our internal HTTP client wrapper. OK to merge?
why: Changed default in shared code; safe-to-merge question.

prompt: Changing the Redis cache key format from user:{id} to u:{tenant}:{id}. Deploying Friday afternoon. What else is relying on the old format that I should worry about?
why: Cache key format change; downstream dependencies.

prompt: This branch changes the /v1/events webhook payload so that amount moves into a nested price object. Which downstream systems or customers could get hurt by that?
why: Serialized format / external consumer impact of a concrete change.

prompt: Write a function that turns ISO-8601 durations like P3Y6M4DT12H30M5S into total seconds (assume 365-day years, 30-day months). I want every case pinned down by a test before the implementation exists.
why: New precisely specified parser; tests first.

prompt: Need a token-bucket rate limiter class: capacity, refill rate per second, try_acquire(n) returns bool, injectable clock. Let's grow it one failing test at a time.
why: New self-contained logic with precise spec, test-driven.

prompt: Build the order status state machine: pending -> paid -> shipped -> delivered, plus cancelled (only before shipped) and refunded (only after paid). Illegal transitions raise. Let the tests drive the code.
why: New state machine with exact rules, tests drive code.

prompt: Implementing the tax calc for invoicing from scratch: progressive brackets (rules attached), round to cents half-even, exemption codes zero out specific line types. Tests come before code on this one please, finance will audit it.
why: New calculation with precise spec, explicitly tests-first.

prompt: I need a semver range matcher supporting ^, ~, >=, <, and || from scratch, no library. Write the expected cases as tests first, then make them pass.
why: New precisely specifiable matching logic, test-first.

prompt: Sarah left 9 comments on PR #412. Go through them and deal with them - a couple I'm pretty sure are wrong.
why: Act on a reviewer's existing comments, including pushing back.

prompt:
CodeRabbit dumped these on my PR:
- 'possible null deref of session in middleware.ts:44'
- 'unused import lodash'
- 'consider memoizing computeTotals'
Fix the ones that are real.
why: Bot review comments to check and apply.

prompt: My lead's review says: 'there's an N+1 in OrderSerializer, and don't swallow the exception in sync_inventory.' Can you handle both?
why: Pasted reviewer notes to act on.

prompt: Ok, take the list of findings from the review you ran earlier and apply them. Flag any that turn out to be false positives once you look at the code.
why: Act on findings from a prior review.

prompt: Reviewer on my Rust PR insists I should use Arc<Mutex<..>> instead of the mpsc channel in the ingest loop. I disagree. Look at the code and either make the change or draft a reply explaining why not.
why: Evaluate a review comment against code; fix or push back with evidence.

prompt: Can you go over PR #88 and look for bugs before I merge it?
why: Near-miss: producing a review, not acting on one.

prompt: Why are ORMs generally slower than hand-written SQL?
why: Near-miss: conceptual performance question, no specific system misbehaving.

prompt: What does ECONNRESET actually mean in Node? I keep seeing it in tutorials.
why: Near-miss: explain an error message, no bug to investigate.

prompt: Design me a REST API for a small library lending system - just list the endpoints and example payloads, I'll take it from there.
why: Near-miss: wants a direct answer, not an interview about decisions.

prompt: utils/date.ts has like 20% coverage. Add unit tests for the existing functions.
why: Near-miss: adding tests to existing code is not test-first development.

prompt: The function I just wrote has duplicated branches and three levels of nested ifs. Tidy it up.
why: Near-miss: quality cleanup of recent changes, not bug-hunting.

prompt: Before release, scan the changes on this branch for injection, authz holes, or leaked secrets.
why: Near-miss: security review of pending changes.

prompt: I'm logging off for the week. Write up where things stand so whoever picks this up Monday isn't lost.
why: Near-miss: handoff-like request is a manual skill; no slash command typed.

prompt: Copilot left six review comments on my PR and I'm not convinced they're right. Take a look at the PR.
why: Boundary rf vs code-review: existing comments to evaluate, not a fresh review.

prompt: Reviewer comment on my PR: 'Does changing how StatusEnum serializes break the mobile clients still on v3?' Respond to that comment - and fix it if she's right.
why: Boundary rf vs blast-radius: an impact question, but it arrives as a review comment to answer and act on.

prompt: Deployed the timezone fix an hour ago but users in Sydney are still seeing yesterday's date on their dashboard. Can you check?
why: Boundary diagnose vs prove-it: the check already failed; the fix did not work, so the cause is unknown.

prompt: Not sure if websockets or SSE is better for our live ops dashboard. Honestly don't quiz me, just hack together a quick SSE version so I can see how it feels.
why: Boundary grill vs just-try-it: user explicitly wants a quick experiment, not questioning; spike is manual-only.

prompt: Add a new 'buy X get Y free' promotion type to the pricing engine. Exact rules: cheapest qualifying item is free, max one free item per X, doesn't stack with percentage coupons. Existing promos must keep working.
why: Boundary tdd vs diagnose: new precisely specified logic, not a bug report.

prompt: Here's my diff to the shared events SDK - it changes publishEvent's signature from (name, payload) to ({name, payload, meta}). Look it over before I merge; mostly I'm worried about the services that import it.
why: Boundary blast-radius vs code-review: concern is downstream consumers of a changed interface, not bugs in the diff.
